question: At a preschool level, the educational team needs to evaluate in everyday contexts the following learning objective from the Natural Environment Exploration core: "Communicate some basic properties of the natural elements they explore, such as colors, textures, sizes, temperatures among others". Which performance of the children would demonstrate the achievement of the selected learning objective?
answer_a: During a learning experience, Santiago draws stones of different sizes
answer_b: During lunchtime, Pablo looks at the spoon and seeing his reflection says: "Look, Pablo!"
answer_c: During an experience in the yard, María collects different types of tree leaves in a basket
answer_d: During free play time in the yard, Soledad rubs some seeds in her hands and says: "Prickly"

question: A first-grade teacher is designing a group activity to work on the skill of exploring along with the class objective: "Identify the senses and their function." To begin the activity, she will give each group a banana, an orange, and a pear, and will ask them to smell, look at, touch, and taste each fruit. Considering the above situation, which of the following activities could the teacher include next so that the students achieve the stated objective?
answer_a: In a worksheet listing the characteristics of each fruit, mark the answers to questions that can be answered using the senses: Which fruit is yellow? Which fruit is sweet? Which fruit is rough? Which fruit is fragrant?
answer_b: In a worksheet where characteristics that can be perceived with some of the senses (sweet/sour, yellow/orange, soft/hard, pleasant smell/unpleasant smell) are indicated, classify the fruits according to these criteria
answer_c: In a worksheet where each sense is represented with an icon, mark the answers to these questions: With which sense did you realize that the banana is yellow? With which that the pear is sweet? With which that the banana peel is smooth? With which that the orange is fragrant?
answer_d: In a worksheet showing the images of these fruits with columns next to them containing a happy face and a sad face, paint your answers to these questions: When eating an orange segment, did you feel pleasure or displeasure? When seeing the color of the banana, did you like it or not? When touching the peel of the pear, did you feel pleasure or displeasure? When smelling the orange, did you like it or not?

question: Through an investigative activity, a teacher wants to address the different techniques for separating mixtures. To this end, she shows her students a jar with water, stones, oil, and salt. The teacher has several jars prepared with the same substances. Which of the following activities would allow students to learn about mixture separation techniques while also developing their skills in evaluating the validity of scientific investigation results?
answer_a: In groups, they determine which technique is most relevant for separating the mixture and then justify their answer
answer_b: In pairs, they separate the mixture using the techniques they deem suitable, and analyze to what extent it was possible to do so
answer_c: Individually, they provide their previous ideas on the procedure to follow, define a collective procedure, and then implement it
answer_d: Individually, they follow a procedure indicated by the teacher to separate the mixture and then identify which separation technique was used in each case

question: A first-grade teacher will begin the unit about the effect of daily cycles on living beings and the environment. Which of the following questions allows the teacher to introduce the content to work with the students?
answer_a: Why does the sun set in the afternoon?
answer_b: Why are the days shorter in the winter?
answer_c: Why do people follow routines during the day?
answer_d: Why do you think most people sleep at night?

question: In the subject of Natural Sciences, a teacher sets the following objective for Grade 1: "Describe what generally happens with fruit trees during the seasons of the year." Which of the following activities is most appropriate to assess students' learning achievement?
answer_a: Provide a blank sheet and ask students to draw their favorite fruit tree in two seasons of the year
answer_b: Provide various images with different types of trees and ask students to classify them into those that have fruits and those that do not
answer_c: Provide a sheet with drawings of fruit trees, where the season each one is in is indicated, and ask them to color them
answer_d: Provide cards with different trees and others with fruits and ask students to associate the tree with the fruit that belongs to it

question: A teacher is working on the human body unit in a 2nd grade class and is addressing the objective of understanding the function of the heart. When inquiring into the students' prior knowledge, he realizes that some have misconceptions about the subject. Which of the following options presents a misconception about the heart?
answer_a: The heart becomes stronger through sports
answer_b: A person's heart is the size of their fist
answer_c: The heart allows blood to carry oxygen to the body
answer_d: The heart produces the blood that goes to the entire organism

question: A group of early years children observe that there are many flowers of different shapes and colors in the yard. The teacher takes advantage of this curiosity and invites them to conduct an investigation on the subject through the following steps: 1. They collect different types of petals fallen in the yard. 2. They compare the shapes and colors of the collected petals. 3. They answer the teacher's question: "What will happen if we put them in water?" 4. They put the petals in a container with water. What scientific thinking skill is the teacher promoting with the question she asks the children during the activity?
answer_a: Experimentation
answer_b: Guided observation
answer_c: Formulation of predictions
answer_d: Comparison of information

question: Read the following situation: An educator invites the early years children to do an experiment. In a bottle, she pours water, oil, and glycerin. Then, she shakes the bottle and shows how the oil and glycerin rise, while the water stays at the bottom. What property of matter is the educator demonstrating in the described experience?
answer_a: Density
answer_b: Solubility
answer_c: Buoyancy
answer_d: Divisibility

question: An educator is explaining to the children the state changes that water undergoes. Which of the following situations can be shown as an example of condensation?
answer_a: The fall of snow on the water of a river
answer_b: The transformation of ice into vapor by the action of the Sun
answer_c: The cooling of sea water and its transformation into ice
answer_d: The moistening of stones exposed to the steam of a geyser

question: An educator shows an image to the children in which the change of state of matter from solid to gas is observed. What is the name of the state change that the educator wants to work on?
answer_a: Condensation
answer_b: Sublimation
answer_c: Evaporation
answer_d: Fusion

question: As part of the unit "My Planet", an educator must explain to the children what elements make up the weather. Which of the following elements should the educator consider in their explanation?
answer_a: Climate, precipitation, and seasons of the year
answer_b: Wind, seasons of the year, and temperature
answer_c: Precipitation, wind, and temperature
answer_d: Climate, wind, and precipitation

question: Consider the following situation: An educator is covering the content about the ocean in the unit on Living Beings and Their Environment. For this, she shows a video in which the sea is seen during a day of swells. One of the children asks why swells occur. Which of the following phenomena should the educator mention as the main cause of the swells?
answer_a: The wind
answer_b: The gravitational force of the Moon
answer_c: The differences in atmospheric temperatures
answer_d: The change in ocean temperatures

question: A preschool teacher shows the children an animated video depicting a phenomenon caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis. This tilt causes the northern and southern hemispheres to be unequally illuminated by the Sun during the Earth's orbit around it. What Earth phenomenon is the educator trying to explain with this resource?
answer_a: Ocean currents
answer_b: The seasons of the year
answer_c: Day and night
answer_d: The tides

question: Read the following situation: In an early years group, Ignacio is presenting about the clownfish and explains to his classmates that this species gains protection from the sea anemone against predators, while the anemone is also protected because the fish drives away other fish that prey on it. The educator intervenes to explain to them what is the name of the type of biological interrelation described by the child. What type of biological interrelation should the educator mention in her explanation?
answer_a: Commensalism
answer_b: Amensalism
answer_c: Neutralism
answer_d: Mutualism

question: A teacher needs their students to understand the meaning of the direction of the arrows in food chains. What content should students understand to achieve their goal?
answer_a: The pyramids of the number of individuals in ecosystems
answer_b: Interspecific relationships
answer_c: Primary and secondary consumers
answer_d: Transformation and conservation of energy

question: In the circulatory system unit, a teacher is working on some technological advances, such as pacemakers, so that his students understand the dynamic and collective nature of science. Which of the following activities deviates from the objective that the teacher wants his students to achieve?
answer_a: Create a pacemaker model in groups following a defined and validated protocol
answer_b: Conduct research on the evolution of pacemakers and design an information sheet
answer_c: Develop an informational panel that provides information on the latest advances in pacemakers
answer_d: Design a timeline that includes the scientists who contributed to what is currently known about pacemakers

question: A teacher aims for her students to understand the inflammatory process as a component of innate immunity. Which of the following prior concepts should the students handle to achieve the objective?
answer_a: Macrophages present antigens to T lymphocytes
answer_b: Neutrophils phagocytize different types of pathogenic agents
answer_c: T lymphocytes specific to a particular antigen undergo cloning
answer_d: B lymphocytes transform into plasma cells that release antibodies

question:
A teacher aims for students to conclude about the relationship between the function of the digestive system and the nutritional needs of cells.
Which of the following evaluation activities would help determine that students have achieved the goal?
answer_a: Propose a hypothesis to determine the relationship between lipases and lipids
answer_b: Develop an experiment on the action of salivary amylase on carbohydrates
answer_c: Analyze the variables of an experiment on the action of pepsin on proteins
answer_d: Analyze a graph about the variation of blood glucose after consuming foods rich in carbohydrates

question: A professor is working on the digestive system unit and would like to explain the role of the microbiota in humans. Which of the following options corresponds to a misconception of students regarding the microbiota?
answer_a: Probiotics correspond to bacteria
answer_b: Bacteria are harmful to living beings
answer_c: The microbiota facilitates the absorption of nutrients in the intestine
answer_d: Antibiotics kill harmful and beneficial bacteria for the body

question: A teacher aims for her students to propose well-founded opinions on some applications of cell biology knowledge. Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to achieve her goal?
answer_a: A presentation that shows the changes cloning techniques have undergone
answer_b: The creation of a poster on techniques for producing transgenic organisms
answer_c: A theoretical research on gene therapy in the treatment of diseases
answer_d: An essay on the use of stem cells in the treatment of diseases

question: A teacher has as a goal for their class that their students understand the process of plasmolysis through an experiment. Which of the following experiments should these students carry out to advance in the understanding of this process?
answer_a: Soak for two hours a piece of potato previously mashed in saltwater and then mash it again
answer_b: Soak for two hours a piece of meat previously mashed in saltwater and then mash it again
answer_c: Soak for two days a carrot previously mashed in distilled water and mash it again after removing it from the water
answer_d: Soak in distilled water an egg from which the shell has been removed and observe the change in volume after three days

question: A teacher wants to evaluate the following learning objective: To explain that living beings are made up of one or more cells and that these are organized into tissues, organs, and systems. Which of the following student learning indicators is directly related to the objective that is to be evaluated?
answer_a: They describe cellular tissues of different systems of the human body
answer_b: They understand that every cell comes from another pre-existing cell
answer_c: They establish relationships between the various levels of organization of organisms
answer_d: They infer relationships between the existence and quantity of cellular structures with the functions of the cell

question: In the context of the unit about plate tectonics and its relationship with continental drift, the occurrence of earthquakes, and the existence of volcanoes, among others, a teacher wants her students to understand that science is a dynamic and collective process over time. Which of the following activities should she ask her students to do as part of a research study to achieve her goal?
answer_a: Analyze the evidence that supports plate tectonics
answer_b: Investigate how the theory of plate tectonics was constructed
answer_c: Explain why it is called the "theory of plate tectonics."
answer_d: Investigate the changes that have occurred in the Earth's crust because of plate tectonics

question: A teacher has designed the following activities for the learning unit related to atomic structure: 1. Students read and analyze a text about the current atomic model and its main characteristics. 2. Students solve problem situations about the conformation of the atom with its constituent elements, its electronic configuration, and its quantum numbers. 3. Students discuss in groups a text about the evolution of the atomic model and its main characteristics with representative diagrams of each (Democritus, Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr). 4. Students make a comparison of the different atomic models indicating their main characteristics. Which of the following sequences promotes progressive learning in understanding atomic structure?
In the context of a "Heat" class, a teacher wants her students to understand the concept of temperature, which of the following contents is a prerequisite to achieve the goal?
answer_a: Kinetic energy
answer_b: Thermal equilibrium
answer_c: Thermal expansion
answer_d: Thermometric scales

question: Marcial reads the following situation to his students: A man is cooking noodles for his family. He boils water in a pot and then puts the noodles in the pot. According to the noodle package instructions, he should lower the flame, but since he is in a hurry, he keeps the fire high because he says that way the water will be hotter and they will cook faster. When discussing his ideas about this situation, most agree with what the man did. Which of the following activities should Marcial propose to his students to challenge their preconceptions?
answer_a: To investigate how the boiling point of water varies under different environmental conditions
answer_b: To measure the time it takes to evaporate 200 mL of water in glasses subjected to flames of different intensities
answer_c: To propose a procedure to analyze the variation of the boiling temperature as a function of the amount of heated water
answer_d: To heat water in a beaker until it boils, increase the flame intensity, and measure the temperature every thirty seconds for four minutes

question: A teacher aims for his students to design an experimental investigation related to the force of friction. For this, he has blocks with different types of surfaces (smooth, with sandpaper, with sponge, with metal) and a table that can be tilted. Students observe that when placing the block on the table and tilting it, at a certain angle, the block begins to slide. Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to evaluate to what extent his students achieve the stated objective?
answer_a: Ask the students to identify the variables of the experiment and determine a method for data recording
answer_b: Provide the students with a work guide to measure the angle at which each block starts to slide and calculate an average for three measurements per block
answer_c: Tell the students to place each block in a fixed position and tilt the table until the block slides, and then measure the angle from which it started to slide
answer_d: Ask the students to determine the steps to establish a possible relationship between the surface of the block and the angle from which it begins to slide

question: A teacher wants to carry out a guided inquiry activity with their students, so that they understand that empirical evidence is fundamental in the construction of knowledge. If the teacher wanted to evaluate the achievement of this goal, which of the following assessment indicators would allow them to do so directly?
answer_a: They interpret the empirical evidence obtained in the experimental stage
answer_b: They record the evidence obtained in the experimental stage of the research
answer_c: They formulate conclusions in which they relate the empirical evidence to the research question posed
answer_d: They design an experiment that allows them to obtain empirical evidence to answer the research question

question: Read the following learning objective: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence supporting the idea that the diversity of organisms is a result of evolution. Which of the following student performances is directly linked to achieving the learning objective?
answer_a: Classify different organisms based on taxonomic criteria
answer_b: Relate the presence of fossils in certain soil layers to past and present conditions
answer_c: Infer, from various fossil records of an organism, the characteristics of that species
answer_d: Compare homologous structures in different species, such as the flipper of a whale and the wing of a bat

question: If a teacher wishes to explain to their students the concept of proto-cooperation, which of the following examples could they use for their explanation?
answer_a: The African hornbill bird houses several insects in its nest, which feed on waste; in this way, they clean up the garbage that accumulates in the nest
answer_b: Ruminants have bacteria in their intestines that are capable of metabolizing cellulose, so that this nutrient becomes available to both
answer_c: Orchids attach to trees to obtain an adequate amount of light, water, and minerals, without taking them from the tree, which is not affected by the orchid
answer_d: Rhizobium bacteria obtain the nutrients they need from the roots of legumes and, in return, the bacteria fix the nitrogen that these plants need

question: A teacher asks his students to analyze the following experimental situation in order to assess whether they recognize the factors that regulate photosynthesis: In an enclosed environment, without windows and at a constant temperature, two plants (A and B) were placed at opposite ends of the room. Plant A is illuminated with green light and plant B with blue light. Both were watered with the same amount of water once a week. Then he asks them to answer the following question: on which of the two plants is greater growth expected to be observed? Which of the following answers will allow the teacher to identify the achievement of the learning objective?
answer_a: Plant A grows more because green photons carry more light energy than blue photons
answer_b: Plant B grows more because blue light can be absorbed by chlorophyll in greater quantity than green light
answer_c: None of the plants grow because despite having water availability, being in a closed space, they do not have CO2 availability
answer_d: Both plants grow in the same way because they have great water availability, which allows them to open their stomata without problem so CO2 can enter

question: A teacher presents her students with the following experimental procedure related to the antigen-antibody relationship: What erroneous preconception allows this experimental procedure to be eradicated?
answer_a: B lymphocytes produce nonspecific antibodies
answer_b: Antigens adapt to only one type of antibody
answer_c: Antibodies can interact with any type of antigen
answer_d: B lymphocytes produce various antibodies when exposed to one type of antigen

question: In the context of planning a class on the endocrine system, which of the following contents is necessary for your students to know in advance so they can differentiate how hormones initiate the response in the target cell?
answer_a: Hormone-releasing factors
answer_b: Chemical nature of hormones
answer_c: Humoral regulation of hormones
answer_d: Feedback mechanisms of hormones

question: In a summative evaluation, the Biology teacher includes the following question: 'What physiological alterations would be observed in a woman who has been administered a drug that blocks the action of GnRH? Describe them.' Which of the following assessment indicators is being addressed with the designed item?
answer_a: Describe the hormonal action responsible for pubertal changes
answer_b: Describe the control of hypothalamic hormones over the ovarian and uterine cycle
answer_c: Describe the sequence of events in the ovarian cycle with reference to the follicular phase, ovulation, and luteal phase
answer_d: Describe the sequence of events in the uterine cycle in relation to menstruation, the proliferative phase, and the secretory phase

question: During the unit related to drugs, a teacher aims for her students to develop the ability to determine the variables of a study. What evaluative activity would allow this teacher to measure the achievement of the stated objective?
answer_a: Construction of a cigarette filter to determine its toxic substances
answer_b: Tabulation of results from a survey constructed by the students on factors influencing early alcohol consumption
answer_c: Construction of a theoretical framework on a research related to the causes of marijuana consumption in adolescents
answer_d: Construction of models built by the students on the mechanisms of action of stimulant drugs at the level of chemical synapses

question: A teacher wants her students to appreciate science as a dynamic process of knowledge construction. To achieve her goal, she asks her students to create a timeline in groups showing the contributions of the following scientists: Friedrich Miescher, Robert Feulgen, P. A. Levene, Frederick Griffith, Oswald Avery, Alfred D. Hershey, and Martha Chase. Which of the following student learning performances is necessary to demonstrate the progress of this knowledge?
answer_a: Interpret images that show different stages of the cell cycle
answer_b: Explain the stages of genetic information flow, from the gene to the protein
answer_c: Explain the DNA molecule model and its relationship with replication and transcription
answer_d: Interpret experiments that show DNA as the molecule carrying genetic information

question: A teacher wants his students to identify genetic alterations that regulate cell proliferation and differentiation in cancer. To do this, he plans the following activities for his students to complete: 1. Build a diagram of the cell cycle and its regulation points. 2. Recognize the concepts of cell proliferation and differentiation using a puzzle. 3. Relate the involvement of key genes in cell cycle control and in different types of cancer. Which of the following options would be a progression from simple to complex of the mentioned activities to achieve the learning objective?

In a senior high school electricity class, a teacher asked her students the following question: "Which of the two bulbs do you think will provide more light?" As a result, all her students answered that the light intensity of bulb B would be higher than that of bulb A. Next, the teacher proposes that they experimentally verify their prediction and discuss the results obtained, comparing them with their original perceptions and conceptions. Regarding the above, what is the objective of the second activity proposed by the teacher?
answer_a: To provoke a cognitive conflict and stimulate conceptual change in the students
answer_b: To evaluate the students' learning related to the functioning of circuits
answer_c: To identify the students' prior ideas related to the functioning of circuits
answer_d: To recognize the causes of the conceptual error manifested by the students in the first activity

question: As part of the unit “Light and Geometric Optics,” a teacher needs to design an activity according to the following objective: “Critically analyze the corpuscular model of light to describe and explain luminous phenomena, understanding that models present advantages and at the same time limitations.” Which of the following activities will allow students to work on the stated objective?
answer_a: Comparatively analyze the diffraction of light in a slit and its polarization when passing through a pair of polarizers, using the corpuscular model of light
answer_b: Comparatively analyze the reflection of a light ray that reflects in a mirror and the diffraction of light in a double slit, using the corpuscular model of light
answer_c: Comparatively analyze the refraction of a light ray that passes through a glass and the reflection of a light ray that reflects in a mirror, using the corpuscular model of light
answer_d: Comparatively analyze the formation of images in curved mirrors and in concave lenses, using the principles of geometric optics, through the corpuscular model of light

question: A teacher is working with her students on the geocentric model proposed by Ptolemy and wants to carry out an activity that allows them to understand how Copernicus's heliocentric model emerged from the critique of the geocentric model. Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to accomplish this purpose?
answer_a: Ask the students to compare, establishing similarities and differences, the models of Ptolemy and Copernicus to describe the Solar System
answer_b: Show the students a computer simulation representing the movement of the Sun and the planets, according to the geocentric and heliocentric perspectives
answer_c: Show the students a video of the retrograde movement of a planet, so that they explain what they observed based on the geocentric and heliocentric models of the Solar System
answer_d: Present the students, from a historical perspective, the implications of what is called the "Copernican revolution", a product of the new vision of the Universe proposed by Copernicus

question: Which of the following activities allows students to critically analyze the principle of conservation of mechanical energy?
answer_a: Using an inclined plane, observe the motion of a sphere rolling over it
answer_b: With the help of an appropriate sensor, record the speed at which a sphere hits the ground when dropped from a table
answer_c: Using a U-shaped track, over which a sphere rolls, observe the maximum height it reaches over time
answer_d: From a computer simulation of a frictionless roller coaster, determine the kinetic and potential energy of a cart that moves along it

question: After studying with her high school sophomores the concept of elastic constant, a teacher proposes the following teaching-learning activity: Students organize themselves into small teams and experimentally determine the elastic constant of a spring, recording their results in a table. Similarly, they determine for which ranges of force the spring obeys Hooke's law. To conclude, they prepare a report in the form of a poster, which is subsequently presented to their classmates. Which of the following scientific research skills can be directly developed through this activity?
answer_a: Evaluate scientific research in order to improve it, considering the validity and reliability of the results
answer_b: Formulate questions and/or problems, based on scientific knowledge, that can be solved through scientific research
answer_c: Explain and argue with evidence from scientific investigations, both orally and in writing, including tables, graphs, models, and ICT
answer_d: Plan various experimental research designs that answer a question and/or problem based on various sources of scientific information, considering the appropriate use of instruments and materials to ensure the collection of reliable data

question: For the unit "Electric Force and Electric Charges" in Twelfth Grade, a teacher wants her students to approach the establishment of laws through the study of the relationship between physical variables. In the context of Ohm's law, which of the following activities is appropriate for this purpose?
answer_a: The students create a graph of current intensity versus voltage for an ideal circuit, considering that the resistance is a constant
answer_b: The students create a graph from a table that records the electrical current intensity in a conductor for different voltages, and then interpret it
answer_c: The students determine the resistance of different conductors; for each case they are given the voltage and current intensity values measured experimentally
answer_d: The students receive different resistors and verify, by applying a determined voltage across each one, whether the resistance reported by the manufacturer is correct

question: As part of an activity in the unit "Heat and Temperature", a teacher proposes the following reading to her Second Year High School students: "In the 17th century, many mining operations had reached such depths that pumping the accumulated water at the bottom had become a serious problem and the pumps that extracted the water had to be powered by horses or people. At this time, scientists like Torricelli or von Guericke made important advances related to atmospheric pressure, the existence of a vacuum, and the so-called "motive power of fire". The first to attempt to build a machine to lift water based on these advances was Papin, although his design was never constructed. More success was had by Savery, who developed a machine where a vacuum was created as the steam condensed. In 1712, Newcomen built a more practical machine, which, by not requiring such high steam pressure, was much safer, and was used for seventy years without requiring substantial improvements. The next step was taken by Watt, who, knowing Black's discoveries about latent heat, had the idea of separating the condenser from the body of the apparatus, constructing the first machine with this design in 1776. Watt's machine, cheaper and more efficient, ended up being used, in addition, in heavy metallurgy and the textile industry. This machine was exported from England to countries aspiring to industrialization, such as France, Germany, and Russia. This technology was the starting point for a revolution that continues to this day and enabled the development of more recent technological applications." Which of the following tasks can students perform from the reading of the previous text?
answer_a: Describe the operation of the steam engine designed by Watt
answer_b: Critically analyze scientific models, seeking their advantages and limitations in describing natural phenomena
answer_c: Develop examples, representations or analogies that allow them to link the contents of Physics with the understanding of everyday world phenomena
answer_d: Indicate how a dynamic and evolutionary process of knowledge construction is accounted for, and whose development is linked to the socio-historical context

question:
In the teaching of Physics, common erroneous preconceptions are recognized, which students have and which affect the learning of new ideas and scientific concepts associated with the topic 'Heat and Temperature.'
Which of the following options does NOT correspond to one of these erroneous preconceptions?
answer_a: Heat is contained in systems
answer_b: Cold is the opposite of heat or its absence
answer_c: Heat implies the presence of two or more systems
answer_d: Heat has temperature as its physical reference magnitude

question: In the context of the unit "Sound" in high school, students are expected to be able to explain why there are differences in timbre between the same note produced by different musical instruments. What concepts are necessary for students to provide a satisfactory explanation of the concept of timbre?
answer_a: Intensity and tone
answer_b: Harmonics and wave superposition
answer_c: Refraction and reflection of a sound wave
answer_d: Frequency and wavelength of a sound wave

question: A teacher wants to evaluate the achievement of the following learning objective by their students: “Formulate explanations about some electrostatic phenomena, such as the electrization of bodies and electric discharges.” Which of the following evaluation indicators is relevant to evaluate this objective?
answer_a: They explain the conditions for electrical conduction in solids, liquids, and gases, citing examples for each case
answer_b: They explain the variables and conditions that determine the magnitude of the electric force between two charges, using Coulomb's law
answer_c: They explain procedures and technologies that protect people from some dangerous electrical phenomena, such as grounding and lightning rods, among others
answer_d: They explain that electrical conductors have electrical resistance and that it depends on their resistivity, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature

question: A teacher seeks to design an evaluative activity for their high school sophomores that allows verifying if they have developed the scientific thinking skill: 'Identify the limitations of scientific models and theories.' In the context of the unit 'Force and motion: motion and its laws', which of the following activities performed by the students will allow the teacher to evaluate the development of the mentioned skill?
answer_a: Design and implement a procedure to measure the acceleration of a body sliding down an inclined plane, comparing its measurements for different angles
answer_b: Conduct an experiment to determine the acceleration with which a body moves in free fall and critically compare the data obtained with theoretical predictions
answer_c: Solve problems of accelerated rectilinear motion, applying the concepts of kinematics and the mathematical relationships between them, to then contrast their results with their previous ideas
answer_d: Calculate fall times, maximum heights reached, and impact speed with the ground, applying the model that describes free fall and vertical launch, contrasting the results with their peers

question: A physics teacher, to conclude the unit "Light", proposes the following evaluative activity to her first-year high school students: Below are two situations in which bulbs of different sizes illuminate a screen. a) Compare the type of shadow that will result on the screen in situations 1 and 2. b) Justify your answer using the corpuscular model of light and geometric optics. What scientific skill can be assessed through this activity?
answer_a: Represent information through scientific models
answer_b: Interpret data from scientific investigations
answer_c: Formulate explanations based on scientific theories and concepts
answer_d: Identify the limitations that scientific models and theories present

question: A teacher is working with their 3rd-year high school students on the concept of specific heat, in the context of the unit Heat and temperature. Which of the following everyday examples allows introducing this concept?
answer_a: Upon taking out a can of drink that has been in the refrigerator for a long time, water droplets form on its surface
answer_b: No matter how strong the applied flame is, the temperature of a pot with boiling water will not increase as long as there is water in the pot
answer_c: After some time of serving a stew, the potato is still very hot to eat, while the meat can be eaten without problems
answer_d: When leaving a bottle painted black and another similar one painted white in the sun, both with water inside, the black one reaches a higher temperature than the white one

question: In the context of teaching polymer chemistry in Middle School, which of the following options would be a sequence that goes from general to more particular?
answer_a: Show examples of monomers, explain how polymers are formed through the corresponding chemical reactions, and then provide examples of natural and artificial polymers used in everyday life
answer_b: Start with examples of polymers used in everyday life (natural and artificial), then explain the formation of polymers through the corresponding chemical reactions, and finally explain what monomers are
answer_c: Provide examples of natural and artificial polymers that are used daily and from them identify the monomeric units; then explain the formation of these polymers through the corresponding chemical reactions
answer_d: Illustrate the chemical reactions that form everyday use polymers and their monomers and then request that, by analogy with the examples, they find other everyday use polymers and develop their chemical reactions

question: What prior learning is necessary for students to develop in order to understand the concept of radioactive series?
answer_a: The structure of the atomic nucleus
answer_b: The atomic constitution of matter
answer_c: The electronic structure of atoms
answer_d: The isotopic composition of an element

question: In a chemistry class, the teacher has proposed that students describe and represent the formation of ionic and covalent bonds. What closing activity will allow the teacher to verify the achievement of their objective?

question: A teacher is working with her 2nd-year Middle School students. As part of her planning, she has considered evaluating the achievement of the indicator "Apply the concept of solution concentration." Which of the following activities directly addresses the indicator?

answer_d: They dissolve different solutes in various solvents and describe the behavior of each solute according to the studied solvent

question: During a class on the main applications of electrochemical cells in the industry, the professor refers to a commercial electrochemical cell called the Downs cell, which allows obtaining metallic sodium through the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (NaCl). question: In the context of studying polyfunctional organic molecules, a teacher is addressing both natural and artificial sweeteners. question: A group of students needs to experimentally identify the presence of functional groups in organic compounds. answer_a: Chromic acid allows only the recognition of ketones

question: Read the following situation: In an elementary grade 1 class a teacher will begin to work on the objective of observing and describing the changes that occur in materials when applying force, light, heat, and water. What topic should the teacher work on before addressing this objective?

answer_d: The action of force, light, heat, or water on different materials

question: A teacher is working on the content of Earth's structure with her 4th grade students and wants to exemplify the Earth's layers through an everyday object. Which of the following objects allows for a clear introduction of the mentioned topic?

question:

answer_a: Prediction

answer_c: They distinguish scientific questions from those that are not

question: Which of the following activities would allow a teacher to know the prior ideas of the students about how volcanic eruptions occur?

question: Which of the following activities will allow students to investigate the main cause of global warming?
answer_a: Summarize a publication in a scientific journal about the effects of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)

answer_d: Analyze scientific reviews containing information related to the effects of thermal inversion on the concentration of pollutant gases

question: A teacher presents the following newspaper headline to his 6th-grade students: 'Environmental pollution in Chile causes more than four thousand premature deaths due to cardiopulmonary diseases.' answer_a: They analyze graphs related to premature deaths from cardiovascular diseases in the last ten years

answer_d: They investigate the reasons why pollution rates increase in winter and the measures that have been taken to reduce these rates

question: A teacher has decided to evaluate whether his students apply the knowledge about nutrition they have learned to their personal reality. What activities are congruent with this objective?

answer_d: In groups, they analyze the results of a survey conducted in their school about eating habits

question: A teacher sets the following learning objective for their class: Explain the relationship between the function of a cell and its parts. Which of the following specific learning objectives proposed for an activity would be consistent with the objective of this class?

answer_b: Compare the organelles and cellular structures that are present in various cell types

answer_d: Relate the different parts of the cell to the contributions of scientists such as Hooke, Leeuwenhoek, Virchow, Schleiden, and Schwann

question: A teacher asks her students to perform the following group work: 1. During the 90-minute period, they must go to the bathroom and collect their urine at 30 minutes, 60 minutes, and 90 minutes. 3. In each time block, they must measure the urine volume with a graduated cylinder; and its density, with a urine test strip. 4. Finally, they must reflect on the components of blood and/or urine based on the results of each individual. answer_a: Data analysis, to study the water balance
answer_b: Data recording, to evaluate the regulation of blood volume
answer_c: Formulation of research hypotheses, to study the hydrosaline balance
answer_d: Control of variables, to expose the effects of different liquids on the concentration of electrolytes in the urine

question: Which of the following options shows a common misconception about changes in matter that students in 7th/8th grade usually have?
answer_a: Chemical changes can be reversible or irreversible
answer_b: Boiling water corresponds to an irreversible change
answer_c: The temperature remains constant when water changes from solid to liquid
answer_d: The mass of a substance remains constant when it undergoes a chemical change

question: A teacher presents the following situation to her students: Suppose we have water at 60°C in one glass, and in another glass we have the same amount of water at 20°C. Next, the teacher asks them to provide arguments for why they think this happened and indicate the assumptions they were based on when making the calculations. Which of the following performances (by the students) does the teacher favor through the learning sequence carried out by the students?
answer_a: Identify the calculation errors made in this type of exercise
answer_b: Analyze the limitations of the model used to make their calculations
answer_c: Identify the procedural errors made during the experimental activity
answer_d: Design an experimental procedure that allows obtaining data more in line with the theory

question: While working with students on the topic of electrical circuits, a teacher notices that one of the students believes that when connecting several identical bulbs in series, the first will shine more than the last because the current 'depletes' as it flows through each successive bulb. Which of the following teacher actions would directly challenge this student's preconceptions?
answer_a: Ask the student to explain in their own words what happens to the current intensity and potential difference in a series circuit
answer_b: Conduct a demonstration experiment where the student can observe the light intensity of bulbs when connected in series
answer_c: Ask the student to measure and compare the current intensities of each bulb connected in series and explain the observations
answer_d: Show a circuit with four bulbs connected in parallel and another with four bulbs connected in series and describe what is observed

question: A student is presented with the following problem: DDT was a widely used insecticide; however, after some years of intensive use, it lost its effectiveness on insects. The student responded as follows: After a period of long exposure to DDT, the insects developed defenses that allowed them and their offspring to be immune to this insecticide. answer_a: The individuals in a population that have advantageous structures or processes will survive and leave offspring
answer_b: The individuals in a population that acquire advantageous mutations will survive and pass on this mutation to their offspring
answer_c: The individuals in a population, in order to adapt to the environment, must develop structures or processes that allow them to survive and leave offspring
answer_d: Most individuals in a population die when competing with those that present advantageous variations, with the latter being the ones that will leave offspring

question: To develop the unit Mechanisms of genetic information conservation, a teacher sets the following learning objective: "Understand that there are mechanisms that allow the conservation of genetic information." Organization of genetic material in the cell. 5. Cell division control points. Which of the following learning sequences will allow the teacher to structure the contents from general to specific?

In an introductory class of the unit 'The Cell', a teacher wants to apply a strategy that allows his students to understand that science is a dynamic process of knowledge construction which development has an impact on society. question: In the implementation of an instructional unit on the electric nature of matter, a teacher organizes the following sequence of activities: 1. The teacher asks students about the origin of electricity and writes the collected responses on the board in a brainstorming session. 3. The students are organized into groups with defined roles and are given: balloons, papers, thread, and rulers. 4. The teacher instructs the students to rub the inflated balloon and the ruler with their hair or a piece of clothing, then bring them close to small objects, like bits of paper and pieces of hanging thread. 5. Students are asked to comment and write down their observations. 6. Finally, they are given time to develop consensual explanations about the origin of electricity. Which of the following options corresponds to a limitation of the activity conducted?
answer_a: Attitudinal content is not addressed
answer_b: The conceptual content worked on is not formalized
answer_c: Scientific thinking skills are not developed
answer_d: Observations are not linked to previous experiences

question: A teacher includes the following exercise in a kinematics test: “A body moves according to the following equation: x=25+40t−5t2 (with t in seconds and x in meters). answer_a: The complexity involved in reading the statements of kinematics problems

answer_c: The insufficient qualitative reflection on the numerical results obtained in kinematics problems
answer_d: The weakness in developing calculation skills to face the resolution of kinematics problems

question: To address the learning objective "Relate the temperature difference to the transfer of thermal energy between different substances," a teacher has his students perform the following activities using two substances. 1. question: The professor aims to promote in her students the ability to select information from the internet for developing research projects. question: In the context of the unit "The atom and its nucleus," a teacher proposes the following activity to their fourth-year high school students: "Debate the implications of studying the atomic nucleus and its possible technological uses, considering that, from what happens in the atomic nucleus of certain elements, it is possible to obtain electrical energy and develop technologies that benefit society. answer_a: Describe the structure of the atom and its nucleus, recognizing the differences between the different elements and their isotopes, and the fundamental forces involved
answer_b: Foster in the students an understanding of the nature of scientific knowledge of the atomic nucleus and the work of nuclear scientists
answer_c: Promote students' interest in connecting the study of the atomic nucleus with its technological applications and everyday life phenomena

question: Read the following learning objective: "Explain light phenomena through experimentation and the use of models, considering the particle and wave models of light." Which of the following evaluation indicators would directly assess the mentioned objective?

question: A teacher proposes to her students the following activity: "Build a model to represent the Earth-Moon system to scale and simulate a solar eclipse using the light of a projector instead of the light of the Sun." answer_a: They show that the Earth, the Moon, and the Sun are aligned, forming a shadow over the Earth
answer_b: They explain that a solar eclipse occurs when the Moon casts its shadow on the Earth's surface
answer_c: They model the orbital movement of the Moon around the Earth over a complete lunar cycle
answer_d: They make a model where both the distance between the Earth and the Moon and their sizes are represented to the same scale

question: A teacher wants to evaluate the ability of their students to formulate the problem of a scientific investigation aimed at determining the factors on which the flotation of a body depends. answer_a: They conduct an experiment to establish the factors that influence the flotation of bodies, proposing appropriate materials and instruments (different liquids, objects of different material, mass, and shape)

answer_c: They use the evidence from the observation of the flotation of bodies in different liquids and from the density measurements, applying logic and constructing an argument for their proposed explanations
answer_d: They formulate a testable hypothesis that relates the flotation of bodies to different variables, such as shape, density, and volume, establishing logical connections between these scientific concepts to guide their experimental design

question: A teacher is starting the unit on chemical bonding and wants to show students that knowledge in chemistry is a progressive, dynamic construction full of controversies. To achieve this, which of the following activities would be relevant?

answer_c: Debate about the demonstration of gas laws
answer_d: Request a bibliographic research on the history of the concept of bonding

question: A teacher in Grade II Secondary presents to their students the equations of the aqueous dissociation of two sodium salts: NaCl(s)+H2O(l)→Na+(aq)+Cl−(aq) NaHCO3(s)+H2O(aq)→Na+(aq)+HCO3−(aq). question:

question: A first-year high school teacher designs the following activity for her students: Take five cups with 50 mL of distilled water and dissolve the following in them: 5 g of salt (NaCl), 5 g of sugar, 5 g of bicarbonate, 5 mL of oil, 5 mL of alcohol. question: In a class on chemical bonds, the teacher aims for students to identify different types of intermolecular interactions and develop scientific skills. Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to verify the achievement of the goal?

answer_b: Ask students to construct a concept map based on reading the intermolecular interactions unit from the textbook
answer_c: Ask students to analyze the presence of intramolecular interactions in natural substances
answer_d: Ask students to design an experimental procedure to identify the presence of different types of intermolecular interactions

question: One of the learning objectives of the Life Sciences curriculum for 2nd Grade aims for students to understand that some animals share physical characteristics, allowing them to be classified within the same group. answer_c: Draw animals according to given characteristics

question: A teacher of a 3rd grade has been working with her students on the objective "Observe and describe, through experimental research, the needs of plants." question: In a preschool, the educator tells the boys and girls that they will conduct an experiment, which involves placing an ice cube in the sun. She tells them that, in silence, each one should draw what they think will happen to the ice cube. Then they go out to the courtyard and she gives each one an ice cube to put in the sun. Back in the classroom, she asks them to draw next to the initial drawing what they actually observed happened to the ice cube. To finish, she asks them to explain how the two drawings are alike and different, and whether what they thought would happen actually happened. answer_a: Recording
answer_b: Prediction
answer_c: Comparison

question: A 6th grade teacher assessed the indicator "Recognize that heat flows from an object with a higher temperature to another with a lower temperature" with the following question: Why do people use thick clothing to keep warm? Upon reading the students' responses, the teacher found that many answered: "Because the clothing reduces the flow of cold to the body." Which of the following activities would help students understand how heat flows between objects?
answer_a: Conduct an experimental activity where students, inside the classroom, touch with their hands a piece of wood, a piece of metal, and a piece of plastic, and record which one feels colder or warmer. Then, they measure and record the temperature of these materials to verify the heat flow
answer_b: Conduct an experimental activity where there is heat flow between two cups of water at different temperatures, demonstrating what happens to the flow when one of the cups is covered with a natural wool sock
answer_c: Conduct an experimental activity by exposing three cups with water at 10°C: one in the sun, another one near a burner, and the last one next to a cup with water at 70°C. Then, they take the time to reach 15°C to verify the heat flow

question: During a class in 8th grade about cellular transport mechanisms, while the teacher is explaining what happens to red blood cells when exposed to a hypertonic solution, a student asks: "What happens to plants when they are not watered and wilt?". Which of the following explanations could the teacher give to the students, in order to maintain scientific rigor and use language appropriate to the mentioned school level?

answer_d: When plants are not watered, the extracellular medium becomes hypertonic, causing water to move from the intracellular medium to the extracellular medium, decreasing the volume of the cytoplasm and causing the central vacuole to contract, which makes the plasma membrane pull away from the cell wall, making the leaves appear wilted

question: In the unit on Microorganisms and Defensive Barriers of the Human Body for 7th grade, a teacher will address the following objective with the students: "Explain the process of immunization caused by vaccines." question: In 8th grade, in the unit on Structure of Matter, a teacher is covering the content of atomic structure. question: A 7th grade teacher has set the following objective for their class: “Explain the behavior of gases in relation to Boyle's law.” What prior knowledge must students have mastered in order to understand this content?
