answer_d: The teacher pronounces the sound of each letter of the word "pala" and the students must recognize which word it corresponds to

question: A teacher sets the following learning objective: "Understand oral texts to obtain information and develop curiosity about the world." Which of the following planned activities to work on this objective considers the students' context?

question: A teacher wants to encourage her students to read poems by focusing on the use of language. answer_d: There is the flower tree, butterfly in suspense beauty distributed, in all directions. Robinson Saavedra

question: During the reading of expository texts, 4th grade elementary students present some difficulties in differentiating between the topic and the main idea. Which of the following explanations correctly establishes this difference?

answer_b: The topic is the conclusion that can be drawn about what the text suggests, and the main ideas are the information that support that conclusion
answer_c: The topic is what the text is going to be about and is discovered because it is in the title, and the main idea is always contained in the first paragraph
answer_d: The topic answers the question “What is the text about?” and the main idea corresponds to what is said about that

question: A teacher is going to evaluate the fluent reading of her 1st grade elementary school students. To do this, she asks them to read the following text aloud: Today is Augustine's birthday. answer_d: They read the complete text respecting the periods that are present

question: For the objective "Express oneself coherently and articulately on topics of interest," 3rd grade elementary school students must orally present for two minutes on a topic of their choice. Which of the following guidelines allows the teacher to evaluate the previous activity?

question: Read the following situation: An educator gives some instructions to the parents to promote reading and writing in children. question: Regarding reading skills, which of the following achievements is expected in a four-year-old boy or girl?

question: Read the following situation: An educator invites children to play with changing letters in some words to form others. answer_a: Lexical awareness

question: Valentina is in preK and has advanced in her writing skills, managing to connect dots to draw different lines, maintaining continuity in the paths. question: A teacher wants students to learn the features of expository text. They are full of above-average amounts of vitamins, nutrients, antioxidants, proteins, enzymes, or healthy fats necessary to maintain health. answer_a: The listing of characteristics of a certain group of foods
answer_b: The description of the effects of consuming a certain group of foods
answer_c: The presence of evaluative judgments alongside the presentation of information
answer_d: The analogy between foods beneficial to health and those we eat daily

question: A 6th grade teacher will assess the following learning objective: "Write short texts of various genres to persuade the receiver." answer_a: Respect the structure of the letter

answer_d: Once the letter is written, read it and check that what you wrote is understood

answer_a: Differentiate homonymous words

question: A teacher will work with her students on reading comprehension skills using a dramatic text. Which of the following activities will allow the students to develop inference skills in understanding the text?

question: To achieve the objective 'Analyze the poems read to enhance their understanding', a teacher performs an activity where they select poems that present literary figures and ask the students to explain them in their own words. question: A teacher is working on the following objective: "Recognize the point of view of the sender of a text." question:

question:

answer_b: The teacher is in favor of the idea that mistakes are normal and unavoidable

question:

answer_d: Identify key words, idiomatic expressions and vocabulary in non-literary texts

question: Read the following classroom situation: One of the learning objectives in English for 11th grade is "to express oneself orally by means of monologues of about three minute extension and dialogues of about sixteen brief and simple exchanges that incorporate communicative functions of previous years and the function of informing what has been said by others, expressing a purpose". answer_a: Because today's learning theories state that oral expression is better developed within a relaxed environment
answer_b: Due to the fact that interrupting a student’s speech for correction inhibits the communicative purpose of the task
answer_c: Since foreign students would always make pronunciation mistakes and they would never eliminate them completely
answer_d: Because making mistakes is part of every learning process and students should be given chances to express themselves freely

question: Read the following classroom situation: The students of 12th Grade B have just finished presenting their dialogues on Dreams, in groups of three. question: In the lyrical genre unit, a teacher presents to his students the following poem: In those days I was twenty years old and I was crazy. I had lost a country but had gained a dream. A wooden room, in shadows, in one of the lungs of the tropics. And sometimes I turned inside myself and visited the dream: a statue eternalized in liquid thoughts, a white worm twisting in love. An unbridled love. A dream within another dream. And the nightmare told me: you will grow up. You will leave behind the images of pain and the labyrinth and you will forget. But in those days growing up would have been a crime. I am here, I said, with the romantic dogs and here I will stay. The romantic dogs, Roberto Bolaño. answer_d: Describe the narrative purpose of the story

question: Once the students have read a micro-story, the teacher asks them to do an activity focused on the critical level of reading comprehension. Which of the following activities would allow for working on this level?
answer_a: Analyze the main ideas of the text
answer_b: Describe what happened to the grandmother’s planet and explain why it is now purple
answer_c: Identify the planets mentioned in the text and describe them based on the story narrated
answer_d: Recognize the conflict present in the story and analyze the message that the text conveys

question: In 7th grade, a teacher is working with students on the concept of polysemy. For this, he hands out a guide containing the following exercise: Read the excerpt and pay attention to the underlined word: Studies show that 35% of mercury pollution is caused by batteries that are incinerated with household waste. To get a sense of the pollution problem, it is enough to mention that a single button cell battery (like those used in watches) can contaminate 6.5 million liters of water, the same amount as an Olympic-sized swimming pool. (Diario El Clarín). Then, he presents the following sentences, which contain the term "battery," and asks them to indicate which one contains the same meaning of "battery" as the previous excerpt. 1. The artillery battery allowed the soldiers to strongly resist the combat. 2. The restaurant chef decided to buy a new set of kitchenware, as the one he used was very worn out. 3. A sober show was provided by the band of musicians in their concert, demonstrating a great level in the use of the drum kit. 4. Batteries pose a real danger to children, so toys that use them must have a safety screw. The students answer that the term in sentence 4 has the same meaning as the excerpt. Why is it appropriate to use this strategy for students to understand polysemy?
answer_a: Because it makes it possible to distinguish words according to criteria of synonymy
answer_b: Because it allows distinguishing the meaning of a term
answer_c: Because it helps to classify words according to their connotation
answer_d: Because it allows grouping vocabulary in a semantic field

question: A Language teacher, aiming for the students to identify the orthographic error, shows a PowerPoint with different texts that contain errors. One of the texts is the following: The teacher asks them about the error in the text, and the students have difficulties identifying it. Which of the following actions would allow the students to identify the orthographic error in the example?
answer_a: Emphasize in class the homographs and find in the example the word that has its pair
answer_b: Emphasize in class the homophones and find in the example the word that has its pair
answer_c: Emphasize in class the polysemous words and find the meanings of the terms present in the example
answer_d: Emphasize in class the paronyms and find the etymology of the terms present in the example

question: In a 6th grade, a Language and Communication teacher will start the following unit: "Correct writing, applying the orthographic rules of the diacritical accent." What learning should students master to understand the diacritical accent?
answer_a: Concept of hiatus
answer_b: Concept of prosodic accent
answer_c: Recognition of monosyllables
answer_d: Recognition of homophonic words

question: During a class dedicated to punctuation marks, a teacher gives the class a text in which quotation marks are used. She then asks the students to explain the specific use of the quotation marks in the following text, based on what they have learned in class: Since constant connectivity is now a widespread reality, always being available on the cell phone has almost become an obligation. Given its wide penetration in the population, ubiquitous usage expectations have developed, as reflected by the fact that for most young people, the off position has been erased from their cultural model of a cell phone. This permanent contact can lead to emotional dissonances because when we send a text message, we expect the recipient to be connected; a delay in response can be considered a personal slight. The cell phone liberates us by providing mobility, but it becomes a tether because we are expected to always be reachable, always "on call." (Javier Serrano-Puche). What prior knowledge should students possess to explain the use of quotation marks in the previous text?
answer_a: Recognize a set phrase
answer_b: Identify a verbatim quote
answer_c: Distinguish levels of formality
answer_d: Reproduce the author's intent

question: Read the following situation: In a 7th grade class, in the Writing section, a teacher is working with his students on the following goal: "Understand different mechanisms of textual cohesion." In order to obtain information about the worked objective, an evaluation containing the following exercise is applied: Read the following fragment and replace the repeated term. Finally, you decided and adopted a cute puppy. But, did you take into account all the care you must have so that the adaptation of the puppy to its new environment is as little traumatic as possible? One of the most complicated issues to solve usually is its care during the night. If the puppy is left alone in the place you have assigned it in your house, as many experts usually advise, it will surely cry incessantly with all its might. Which of the following assessment indicators corresponds to the exercise of the evaluation?
answer_a: They distinguish the communicative adequacy presented by the text
answer_b: They recognize the coherence of a text
answer_c: They apply synonymy as a coreference resource
answer_d: They distinguish semantic relations between connectors

question: A 5th-grade teacher whose class goal is to work with students on applying the concept of a semantic field, proposes reading the following fragment: The vegetation landscape of the Metropolitan Region is characterized by being predominantly mountainous, although in the valleys and basins the acacia steppe develops. In this region, there is a strong retreat of native vegetation due to high urbanization. Due to the high degree of population that the region presents, the landscape has been altered, significantly reducing the natural vegetation, remaining only on the slopes and mountain foothills. Agriculture and forest plantations of exotic species, such as eucalyptus, poplars, and pines, have transformed the region's agricultural landscape. Above 500 meters of altitude, there are sclerophyllous forests characterized by their hard, evergreen foliage that requires greater precipitation (between 400 and 1000 mm) to develop. (National Library of Congress). Using the above fragment, which of the following activities carried out by students would be the most appropriate to work on the above objective?
answer_a: Recognize examples of synonymy in the text
answer_b: Investigate the meaning of unknown terms
answer_c: Classify words from the text based on a hyperonym
answer_d: Group words from the text according to their grammatical category

question: In a Language class, to apply the concept of "propaganda", the teacher asks the students to create a campaign that promotes environmental care within the school. For this, various tasks are assigned, such as identifying the school's situation regarding environmental care, planning the campaign's objectives, formulating a creative strategy, and seeking the technical resources to carry out the project. To monitor the fulfillment of the first stage of the campaign, the teacher gives each group a checklist so they can self-evaluate. Why is it appropriate to use a checklist in this first stage of the campaign?
answer_a: Because each student will be able to know how they are performing in the assigned tasks
answer_b: Because the students will be able to categorize the activities they have completed
answer_c: Because the students will be able to analyze in detail each of the actions they have carried out
answer_d: Because the students will be able to verify if they have completed the proposed tasks related to the campaign

question: In a 7th grade class, a teacher designs an instrument to evaluate the expansion of her students' vocabulary. Which of the following indicators shows that the students are correctly addressing vocabulary expansion by using strategies to determine the meaning of new words?
answer_a: They replace repeated terms with synonyms
answer_b: They highlight new words and define them according to the context
answer_c: They look up the meaning of different words in the dictionary
answer_d: They make sentences using synonyms of unknown words

question: Seventh grade students are working on the formal structure of a news article, and for this, the teacher has asked them to produce a news text. Which of the following evaluation instruments is most appropriate to verify the presence of the news article's structural elements in the produced text?
answer_a: Appreciation scale
answer_b: Checklist
answer_c: Anecdotal record
answer_d: Observation guideline

question: In an 8th grade class, during the unit on epic poetry, a teacher designs an instrument to evaluate the following learning objective: 'Understand the production context in which the epic is framed.' Which of the following assessment indicators shows that students are addressing the stated learning objective?
answer_a: Physically and psychologically characterizes the hero of the epic
answer_b: Describes the cultural traits of the people to which the epic refers
answer_c: Describes the values that the epic exalts with importance to divine interventions
answer_d: Recognizes the didactic sense of the epic, considering its moralizing significance for society

question: A teacher aims for his students to identify the purpose of using dialogical sequences in different narratives. To do this, he proposes reviewing different texts, including reading the following fragment: Also the poet, if he is a true poet, must perpetually repeat "I don't know". With each verse he tries to answer, but at the moment he puts the final period, doubts assail him and he begins to notice that his answer is temporary and in no way satisfactory. Then he tries again and again, so that the successive signs of his dissatisfaction with himself are held together with a huge clip by literary historians to call them "The Work." Sometimes I fantasize about improbable situations. I imagine, for example, in my audacity, that I have the opportunity to talk with Ecclesiastes, the author of a shocking lament about the vanity of all human enterprises. I would have bowed very deeply before him, as he is -at least for me- one of the most important poets. But then I would have taken him by the hand: "There is nothing new under the sun," you wrote, Ecclesiastes. Nevertheless, You yourself were born new under the sun. And the poem you created is also new under the sun, as before You nobody had written it. [...] And also I would like to ask you, Ecclesiastes, what would you like to write now, again under the sun? Something with which to complete your ideas, or maybe you're tempted to deny some of them? [...] For you will not say "I have already written everything, I have nothing to add." No poet can say this, much less one as great as You. (I don't know, Wislawa Szymborska.) Of the following questions posed by the teacher, which one enables students to recognize the purpose of the dialogical sequence in the previous fragment?
answer_a: What register of speech does the broadcaster use to address Ecclesiastes?
answer_b: What are the central themes addressed in Ecclesiastes' book according to the broadcaster?
answer_c: What is the contrast that can be drawn between literary historians and Ecclesiastes?
answer_d: What is the relationship between Ecclesiastes' reference and the idea of the transient nature of the poet's certainties?

question: A teacher is working in the Writing section with the aim of expanding the vocabulary of unfamiliar concepts. For this, she proposes her students read the following fragment: The processes of deinstitutionalization, desocialization, depoliticization, and the blurring and fragmentation of social imaginaries constitute the basis of attitudes of apathy, participation crisis, marked individualism, and disbelief, which ultimately leads young people to a prior abandonment of citizenship. ("The social issue of youth," Pérez, G. and Romero, M.) Which of the following activities could best address the stated objective?
answer_a: Develop a semantic field based on the concept of citizenship
answer_b: Search for the meaning of frequently used Latin expressions such as "a priori" for students to use in their writings
answer_c: Look for the meaning of the prefix "des" and apply it to words in the fragment
answer_d: Underline the concepts that are most difficult in the reading and infer their meaning according to the context

question: Read the following situation: A teacher, whose objective of the class is to understand argumentative texts, presents the following editorial to the students: The young people rise up “Don't shoot me. I'm trying to study.” “We want a graduation, not a funeral.” Hundreds of thousands of students in the United States have risen up with slogans like this against the status quo of the arms industry that, in alliance with the individualistic and colonizing spirit that forged the country, has gained a power without too many limits. Hundreds of thousands of young people marched on Saturday on Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington between the White House and the Capitol in a “March for our Lives” supported by 800 other protests across the country. Their reading of manifestos in front of the legislators' headquarters also aimed to mark the target of their proposals: the seat of Congress. They try to focus the national political debate on gun limits several months before the elections that will renew the House of Representatives, a third of the Senate, plus the majority of state governors. Thus, the pressure grows in the streets, but it has not yet managed to make a dent in the Government. President Trump signed a budget hours before the marches that does not include special measures to curb violence. The challenge for young people is colossal, but only their persistence can make the premise that the future is in their hands a reality. (El País Newspaper). Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to begin work on understanding the editorial?
answer_a: Identify the discursive modalizers present in the editorial
answer_b: Recognize the different types of arguments present in the editorial
answer_c: Search for information on the social and political context to which the editorial refers
answer_d: Mark in the editorial the unknown words and look them up in the dictionary

question: Read the following situation: A teacher is working with a senior class on the following learning objective: “Recognize the phenomenon of perspectivism in contemporary literary works.” To achieve this, she presents her students with the following excerpt from the novel The Cubs by Mario Vargas Llosa: He only returned to school after the Independence Day holidays and, oddly enough, instead of having been deterred by soccer (wasn't it because of soccer, in a way, that Judas bit him?) he came back more athletic than ever. On the other hand, he started to care less about his studies. And it made sense, no fool he, he no longer needed to cram: he'd show up for exams with very low averages and the Brothers would pass him, bad exercises and excellent, poor homework and he passed. Since the accident they pampered you, we'd say, you knew nothing about fractions and, such nerve, they gave you a sixteen. Besides, they made him help in mass, Cuéllar reads the catechism, carries the year's pennant in processions, erases the blackboard, sings in the choir, hands out the notebooks, and on the first Fridays he would have breakfast even if he did not take communion. Who like you, Choto said, you live the good life, shame that Judas didn't bite us too, and he wasn't afraid of you: the Brothers pampered him fearing his father. (The Cubs, Mario Vargas Llosa). What sequence of activities would be appropriate to begin addressing the proposed objective?
answer_a: Dramatic reading, underline the names of the characters in the text and summarize the stance of each one
answer_b: Individual reading as a first approach to the text, identify the idioms used by the characters and rewrite the text replacing those terms
answer_c: Characterize the characters and identify their role in the story and paraphrase the content of the text to recognize its central idea
answer_d: Analyze the text based on a questionnaire about the main ideas, identify the textual cohesion markers, and write a comment about the conflict in the text

question: A professor who is working on the characteristics of contemporary narrative wants to check the learning of narrative techniques that affect the time of the story. To do this, he proposes his students read the following narrative fragment: As for me, I will be shot as a torturer and murderer. The court has proceeded with rectitude; from the beginning, I have declared myself guilty. Tomorrow, when the prison clock strikes nine, I will have entered death. (Deutsches requiem, Borges, J.L.). Regarding the treatment of time in the previous fragment, the teacher asks his students what feature they visualize and they mostly respond with an analepsis. What pedagogical action by the teacher would allow the students to get out of this confusion?
answer_a: Provide examples with short stories of the differences between flashback and racconto
answer_b: Practice recognizing cataphoric textual relationships in texts
answer_c: Provide examples with contemporary narrative fragments of the characteristics of historical referential time
answer_d: Reinforce through a presentation the characteristics that distinguish anticipation narration

question: Read the following situation: A teacher, in a senior high school class, asks her students to write an argumentative text and then underline all the connectors used in the text. One of the students wrote the following paragraph: A concrete advantage of using bicycles as a means of transportation is that they help to reduce traffic congestion and the space they take up on streets and parking lots. For this reason, their use compared to other means of transportation also has some disadvantages, such as the increased time spent getting to work, the need to carry a change of clothes, physical effort, or greater exposure to weather conditions. In which of the following connectors does the student have difficulty in terms of use and why?
answer_a: For this reason, because they use it as an adversative connector
answer_b: Like, because they use it as an exemplification connector
answer_c: Or, because they use it disjunctively for sentences that are not opposed
answer_d: And, because they use it excessively in lists of analogous elements

question: A teacher proposes that the class write an expository text with the objective of making students aware of the writing process, identifying their strengths and weaknesses in terms of idea organization and drafting. Which activity would directly address the stated objective?
answer_a: Propose the reading of various expository texts with the aim that they serve as models for the composition of their texts
answer_b: Suggest a peer review session using a rubric that allows students to develop a critical view of writing and take responsibility for feedback
answer_c: Provide, along with the text, a checklist that allows students to verify their texts meet requirements such as spelling, coherence, and cohesion
answer_d: Ask students to create a preliminary document that serves as an outline to organize the information they will develop in their writings, distinguishing the main ideas from those that will support them

question: Read the following situation: To address the learning objective: "Write an argumentative text", the teacher instructs students to freely choose a topic related to the use of technology in education, then investigate the topic they selected and write a text in which they develop their point of view. The students prepare a first draft of their writing and submit it to the teacher for an initial review. From the following feedback options provided by the teacher, which is most effective to achieve significant improvements in rewriting the text?
answer_a: Highlight in the text the sentences or paragraphs that need to be reworked by the student
answer_b: Underline connectors that indicate thematic progression, so that they delve into those topics
answer_c: Write brief comments in the text, such as: "It's confusing", "It's adequate", "This needs improvement", so that the student can rectify it
answer_d: Provide observations in the text such as: "Are the arguments offered with the purpose of confirming or refuting the thesis?"

question: Read the following situation: In a class on the analysis of argumentative texts of a third year of high school, whose learning objective is 'Understand the point of view of a speaker, their reasoning and the use of rhetorical resources', the teacher proposes to the students to read and compare letters to the editor on the same topic. Which of the following evaluation indicators addresses the learning objective proposed for the class?
answer_a: Identify the thesis of various texts, considering the use of semantic and syntactic resources
answer_b: Compare the thematic progression of different texts based on the arguments and linguistic resources used
answer_c: Develop a personal response to the topic presented in various texts, using coherence and cohesion resources
answer_d: Distinguish the main ideas, considering the linguistic resources used, to identify the purpose of the text

question: Read the following situation: A high school teacher will assess the narrative genre unit with a final project that consists of analyzing a short story, distinguishing the following elements: – Type of literary world. – Temporal resources. – Type of setting. – Characterization of characters. – Type of narrator. Given the nature of the evaluation of this unit, what instrument should the teacher apply to assess and provide feedback on the work?
answer_a: Holistic rubric
answer_b: Analytical rubric
answer_c: Appreciation scale
answer_d: Checklist

question: In reading a story, which of the following options corresponds to a reading strategy inherent in the holistic model?
answer_a: Underline the words in the story that represent the actions of the characters
answer_b: Classify the characters in the story as main or secondary
answer_c: Infer what the text is about based on its illustrations or other linguistic clues
answer_d: Sequence the main events of the story according to their order in the narrative

question: A 4th-grade teacher divides the class into groups and asks them to write an instructional text to teach an invented game to their classmates. What activity would be appropriate to evaluate the communicative suitability of the texts produced by the students?
answer_a: Exchange the texts with another group and ask them to check if a single idea is developed for each step of the game
answer_b: Exchange the texts with another group and ask them to underline the actions contained in each step that are not in imperative mode
answer_c: Exchange the texts with another group and ask them to check if the title placed is consistent with the steps described to develop the game
answer_d: Exchange the texts with another group and ask them to play while recording the successes and difficulties they had in developing the game

question:
A teacher is working with his third-grade students on reading comprehension based on the legend "The Solitary Condor." Below is an adapted excerpt from this text:
A long time ago, it was arranged that all the birds of the coastal mountain range should get married. To that end, notices were put up everywhere so that the birds would gather for the event. There were only a few minutes left to start the ceremony and all the birds were eagerly waiting for the anticipated moment, but the condor had no one to marry. Disappointed, he left. The marriages took place; the birds celebrated, although they never forgot the sadness of the condor.
One of his students asks the teacher: What does “disappointed” mean?
Which of the following activities would help the student understand the meaning of this word through the recognition of its prefix?
answer_a: Look for the word that is part of its lexical family in the text and relate both words with the clues in the text that allow deducing its meaning
answer_b: Look for other words in the text that contain affixes, underline them and relate them to determine what these words have in common
answer_c: Look for the words that characterize the condor in the text, underline them and relate them to the word whose meaning you want to find out
answer_d: Look for the action that continues the word whose meaning you want to find out and relate these two words with the information that is close in the text

question: A teacher from a 4th grade class has divided the class into groups to write a news article on different topics. Once they have written the body of the article, he observes the headlines each group is creating and notices that one of them wrote: “The zoo lion”. Seeing this, he decides to propose an activity to help them review and evaluate their headline. Which of the following activities is most suitable for this group of students to review and improve their headline according to the specific characteristics of this element of the news?
answer_a: Read with them the headlines of the news written by the other groups. Then, hand out the bodies of those articles and ask them to match each headline with the corresponding body
answer_b: Read with them bodies of newspaper articles. Then, ask them to associate the headlines of these articles and discuss with their classmates how they knew these fragments matched the headlines
answer_c: Read with them headlines of different news articles, such as: “Polar bear dies at the zoo”, “Albino rhino is born in Chile”. Then, ask them to distinguish the elements present in those headlines that are missing from theirs
answer_d: Read with them the article they wrote. Then, ask them to take up the written headline and complete it by adding information, based on questions such as: “Where is the zoo located?”, “What is the lion like?”

question: A 4th grade basic education teacher is working with her students on understanding the grammatical agreement between the subject and the verb. For this purpose, she has decided to incorporate some activities during the reading of a short text that presents a single protagonist. Which of the following activities would be appropriate for the teacher to incorporate so that students work on the grammatical agreement between the subject and the verb?
answer_a: Underline the actions performed by the protagonist and rewrite them by changing the number of the subject
answer_b: Select in the text the sentences where the protagonist appears and distinguish the subject from the predicate in each one
answer_c: Highlight with different colors in the text the actions performed by the protagonist and conjugate them in a different tense
answer_d: Enclose with a color the subjects of the sentences where the protagonist appears and replace them with the corresponding personal pronoun

question: A teacher of a 4th Grade class will start working on the function of the adverb with his students, so they can use them in their writings. As they have been working on reading comprehension from the story 'El Gatopato y la princesa Monilda' by María Elena Walsh, the teacher decides to select the following fragment of that text for his activity: For many days, Gatopato spent crying all the time in a shoe because he felt that nobody loved him. One day, Princess Monilda passed through the forest and saw him. She thought he was cute and wanted to have a Gatopato for a long time. So she gently picked him up, petted him, and took him to the palace. Which of the following tasks allows students to understand the function of the adverb from the fragment selected by the teacher?
answer_a: Explain why Gatopato was sad
answer_b: Underline what Monilda thought when she saw Gatopato
answer_c: Describe the way Monilda picked up Gatopato
answer_d: Identify where Gatopato spent many days crying

question: An educator intends to carry out a diagnostic evaluation of oral language for a group of preschool children. To do this, she greets the group and invites the children to describe the activities they did over the weekend. Considering the children's age, which of the following stories indicates difficulties in oral expression?
answer_a: “First we went to see my aunt Tantisca. Then to the piazza to play.”
answer_b: “I watched a movie with my dad. We went to the cinema. Then I had ice cream with your sister.”
answer_c: “I went to the beach, we made sand castles. There were people sunbathing and running.”
answer_d: “I went with my mom to a super big park. There was a game to climb high.”

question: A kindergarten teacher is conducting a presentation activity by the children, on a region of Chile; through this strategy, she is gathering evidence on the ability of the children to "Orally communicate topics of their interest, using varied vocabulary and incorporating new and relevant words to different communicative situations and interlocutors." Sofía presents the Region of La Araucanía and indicates that in it there are sheep and they are generally with their friends. Considering the previous situation, what intervention by the teacher would help Sofía achieve the stated learning objective?
answer_a: Thank you, Sofía, you shared important information about La Araucanía. What else did you learn about the sheep?
answer_b: Thank you, Sofía, the information you shared is very interesting. Do you know what sheep like to do with their friends?
answer_c: Thank you, Sofía, the information you shared is very interesting. Do you know what other animals are in La Araucanía, besides sheep?
answer_d: Thank you, Sofía, you shared important information about La Araucanía. Do you know what a group of sheep is called? Flocks can also be of goats

question: In relation to the initiation to writing, which of the following educational situations is most suitable for promoting that children gradually produce their own graphic signs?
answer_a: That they copy short messages to record the results of their activities
answer_b: That they draw and write in their sketchbook every day on topics of their interest
answer_c: That they have laminated cards to freely practice arabesques and garlands
answer_d: That they complete sequences of dots in worksheets, respecting the start and end points

question: Which of the following performances corresponds to that of a boy or girl who is in the syllabic-alphabetic stage of writing?
answer_a: Copies their name
answer_b: Writes familiar words
answer_c: Writes separate letters they know
answer_d: Copies simple phrases to communicate something

question: A preschool teacher plans to work with her group on the following learning objective: "To discover, in playful contexts, phonological attributes of known words, such as identifying final sounds." Which of the following learning experiences is the most appropriate to work on the objective set by the teacher?
answer_a: Guess words that will be mentioned phoneme by phoneme
answer_b: Discover words that form assonant rhymes within a poem
answer_c: Physically represent the number of syllables in different words
answer_d: Identify words that have the same sounds in different alliterations

question: The Learning Resource Center of a school has various didactic materials to promote language development. A teacher of preschool must select a resource to work on syntactic awareness with her group of boys and girls. Considering the previous situation, what is the most appropriate resource to directly work on the development of syntactic awareness?
answer_a: Sheets with verbal opposites
answer_b: Domino of initial vowel sound
answer_c: Cards for image-word association
answer_d: Cards to build sentences with pictograms

question: A preschool educator, after completing the first semester, observes that, in artistic languages, kinesthetic skills have been addressed very little compared to other skills. To reverse the situation, she decides to implement, after the reading of stories, experiences that promote them. According to the situation read, what is the most appropriate experience to promote the aforementioned skills in young children?
answer_a: Represent the story with puppets
answer_b: Model the space where the story takes place with playdough
answer_c: Play to personify the characters of the story bodily
answer_d: Draw the moments and characters they liked the most from the story

question: A teacher in a Grade 8 class addresses the production of texts with an informative purpose, considering the correct application of punctuation spelling. For this, the teacher asks the students to write a text. During the monitoring of the writing activity, the teacher reviews the following fragment from one of the students: "The origin of the universe according to what the experts say is still a mystery." What should the student practice to overcome the difficulty observed in their text regarding the use of commas?
answer_a: Recognition of vocatives
answer_b: Recognition of explanatory clauses
answer_c: Recognition of conjunctive conjunctions
answer_d: Recognition of adversative coordinated sentences

question:
A teacher in a 6th grade class asks the students to write short narrative texts to sequence events and evaluate the spelling of written production. Upon reviewing the progress of the writing, she notices that a student has written: The red-haired girl always helped her classmates with their tasks with the best intentions; however, her friends continuously told her that she was becoming invasive.
Which of the following interventions by the teacher would more directly enable the student to understand her mistake and improve her spelling?
answer_a: Read examples and explain the rules for the use of 's'
answer_b: Show the student how the word 'invasive' is spelled, so she can correct her mistake
answer_c: Indicate to the student the graphemic correspondence between 'c' and 's' using examples
answer_d: Point out that the word 'invasive' is related to 'invade', therefore, there is a mistake in the way she wrote the word

question: A teacher in 8th grade conducts a summative assessment of a reading of a dramatic genre. Despite the fact that the work was analyzed in class, the result of the assessment shows that the majority of the students did not manage to understand the dramatic conflict of the work read. What initial action would allow the teacher to better address the difficulty that the students present?
answer_a: Propose to the students an activity in which they describe the resolution and the ending of different dramatic works
answer_b: Ask the students to analyze the most tense moment of various dramatic works, where the conflicting forces face each other
answer_c: Have the students analyze the dialogue of characters from different dramatic works where the situation of the confronting forces is revealed
answer_d: Review, together with the students, the evolution of the main characters in various dramatic works and how they relate to other characters

question: A non-teaching staff member, in an 8th-grade class during the unit on the lyric genre, proposes as an activity to characterize the lyrical speaker in the following poetic fragment by Miguel Hernández: I am called mud although Miguel calls me. Mud is my profession and my destiny which stains with its tongue whatever it licks. I am a sad instrument of the road. I am a tongue sweetly infamous before the feet that I idolize spread out. After reading the previous poetic fragment, the teacher asks the students the following question: Who is the lyrical speaker? Several students respond that the speaker coincides, in this case, with the author of the poem, Miguel Hernández, since he himself declares it by saying that his name is Miguel. What answer from the teacher could make the difference between the author and the lyrical speaker more understandable to the students, based on the previous poetic fragment?
answer_a: Although the speaker of the poem confesses to being named Miguel, just like the author of the poem, Miguel Hernández, nothing assures us that it is exactly the same person
answer_b: The author of the text differs from the lyrical speaker in that the poem constitutes a fiction whose internal mechanics do not depend on extra-literary reality, even if similarities can be found between the two planes
answer_c: Beyond the similarities that may exist between the lyrical speaker and the author's biography, the voice speaking in the poem is always a verbal construction, not a flesh-and-blood person, so author and speaker are never the same
answer_d: The lyrical speaker is not the same as the author because the reality to which the 'I' refers is a reality of discourse, which only holds value in the instance in which it is produced and does not have linguistic existence beyond the speech act that proclaims it

question: A teacher in a 7th Grade class asks the students to write a news article about the school's anniversary week. The following is a fragment of a draft of the text written by one of the students. The Blue Alliance, after a close result, is the winner of the anniversary week. After a week of intense competitions, the Blue Alliance took first place in the 2017 anniversary. With a difference of only 100 points, the diligent Blue Alliance was crowned champion of the anniversary of the San Patricio school last week. Among the activities won by the Blue Alliance, the most outstanding was the dance of the kings, presenting a great choreography: the most coordinated, creative, and motivating of all. The 4th-year high school students, with great enthusiasm and joy, led the celebration of the victory and invited the other members of the Alliance to dance and sing with them. Considering the characteristics of the news article, what is the difficulty presented by the text written by the student?
answer_a: The description of the facts provides irrelevant data
answer_b: The headline does not convey the central idea of the news
answer_c: The ideas presented lack precision and conciseness
answer_d: The sender of the message does not distance themselves from the facts narrated

question:
A teacher designs an instrument to evaluate the production of an informative article about the historical context of an epic.
Which of the following indicators allows for evaluating the writing process, specifically the coherence of the informative article?
answer_a: Fulfill the purpose of informing about the historical context of the epic
answer_b: Present the information in independent paragraphs that address the historical context of the epic
answer_c: Establish meaningful connections between the ideas that address the historical context of the epic
answer_d: Provide descriptions that include relevant information about the historical context of the epic

question:
A teacher, in the unit of the lyric genre in an 8th Grade class, will conduct a summative evaluation, which contains, among other questions, the following: What is the tone of the following poem?
Despecho
Ah, I am so tired! I have laughed so much,
So much, that tears have appeared in my eyes;
So much, that this grimace that contracts my mouth
Is a strange trace of my wild laughter.
So much, that this intense pallor I have
(Like in old noble portraits)
Is due to the fatigue of the wild laughter
That slides its lethargy over my whole body.
Ah, I am so tired! Let me sleep;
For, like anguish, joy makes you sick.
What a strange occurrence to say that I am sad!
When have you seen me more joyful than now?
Lie! I have no doubts, nor jealousy,
Nor uneasiness, nor anguish, nor sorrows, nor longings,
If my eyes shine with the humidity of tears,
It is due to the effort of laughing so much...
Juana de Ibarbourou
Upon reviewing the evaluations, the teacher finds the following student's response: “The tone of the poem is joy, because the speaker says in several verses that they are laughing.”
What comment from the teacher to the student's answer could favor their identification of the tone of the evaluated poem?
answer_a: You must explain what the speaker means in the last stanza of the poem, where they establish their stance, and then identify the tone
answer_b: You managed to grasp that the poem talks about joy. However, the tone still needs to be determined. To do so, I suggest you relate the title to the content of the poem
answer_c: You identified that the emotion of the poem relates to joy, but you did not recognize the tone. You must identify the lyrical attitude and relate it to the poem's purpose
answer_d: You remained at a denotative level, failing to recognize the tone of the poem. You must underline the verses where a feeling is explicitly mentioned in the poem to determine which one prevails

question: During the narrative unit in a 6th grade class, a teacher asks the students to write a short expository text about some animal and its characteristics. One of the students writes the following text: Pandas are cute and chubby. I like them because they are funny and lazy, they like to sleep just like me. The other day I went to the zoo and saw a very cute one, but I felt sorry because it was locked in a small cage and looked sad. Which of the following teacher's comments on the student's text would provide better formative feedback and help guide the student's learning?
answer_a: You wrote a short text, but it's a subjective commentary, not an expository text; it does not adhere to objective information
answer_b: Review the guide on expository text and summarize the characteristics of this type of text. Then, write a new expository text
answer_c: Expository texts do not use the first person, nor include adjectives with personal judgments. Your text has personal judgments
answer_d: You managed to identify an animal. You should write about its characteristics: where do pandas live, what is their anatomy, what do they eat, what size are they?

question: In a 6th Grade class, in the unit on the lyric genre, a teacher will give the students a written test, which includes a section in which the understanding of the language used in different poems will be evaluated. Which of the following evaluation indicators would address the evaluated learning?
answer_a: They identify the lyrical motive of the poem
answer_b: They recognize the lyrical attitude of the speaker of the poem
answer_c: They explain the allusions of the verses of the poem in denotative and connotative terms
answer_d: They specify the elements and verses of the poem that help recreate a mood

question: A teacher in a 7th grade class, in the unit on argumentation, will evaluate the following learning objective: "To value the diversity of perspectives, beliefs, and cultures present in their environment", through conducting a debate. Which of the following options presents the evaluation indicator that best responds to the stated learning objective?
answer_a: They ask others about their position or opinion on a topic
answer_b: They counter-argue using solid data based on reliable evidence
answer_c: They ask questions and make comments, out of their own motivation, to delve deeper into a topic
answer_d: They intervene with respect towards the heterogeneous opinions expressed by their peers

question:
For a 12th grade class, during the unit "Reality and Freedom", a teacher, in order to develop an interpretative analysis of a poetic text from a formal level, gives her students the following poem to read:
"I would be less punished if your complexion were not nardo for my sight, nardo, your skin thistle for my touch, thistle, your voice your era for my ear, your era. Your era is your voice for my ear, your era, and I burn in your voice and around you I burn, and I take time to burn what I take time to offer you my era, my voice for yours my era. Your hand is a thorn if I feel it, thorn, wave your body if I reach it, wave, close once, but a thousand not close. Heron is my sorrow, slender and sad heron, alone like a sigh and an I, alone, stubborn in her error and in her disgrace stubborn." From The Unceasing Ray, by Miguel Hernández.
Which of the following questions asked by the teacher to the students is related to an interpretative analysis from the formal level of the text?
answer_a: To whom is the lyrical speaker addressing, and what characteristics do they present?
answer_b: To what traditional strophic form does the structure of the poem correspond?
answer_c: What meaning does the heron acquire in the last stanza, in relation to the lyrical speaker?
answer_d: What is the relationship between what the speaker says and the sounds that are repeated throughout the poem?

question: In a first year high school class, a teacher proposes the following activity to students to work on vocabulary expansion: “Read the following report, which was written last year by a student after the integrated field trip activity, and replace the highlighted terms with the words noted following the text”. We had never heard the sound of a partridge when it is chased or harassed. The sound of the geese was somewhat harsh, but the sound of the turkeys was, without a doubt, the most impressive. We did not know how to distinguish the usual song of hens and the noise they make when they are ready to brood. However, by far, the most beautiful thing we heard was the song of the swallows. Truly beautiful. Supporting words: honk – cluck – quack – gobble – chirp – cackle. To which objective related to vocabulary expansion does the previous activity correspond?
answer_a: Use precise vocabulary
answer_b: Take advantage of the polysemic use of words
answer_c: Recognize the meaning of a term in context
answer_d: Incorporate technical vocabulary from readings

question: A teacher wants to work on the writing of a dramatic play in 1st Grade of secondary school. For this purpose, she asks the students to read a news article and then write a short play in three acts based on the theme of the article. Considering the stages of the writing process, which of the following pedagogical actions best guides the construction of the play's conflict?
answer_a: Guide the planning process oriented towards the construction of the dramatic conflict
answer_b: Guide, during the self-correction stage of the play, the identification of the dramatic conflict
answer_c: Guide the construction of the conflict during the review, modeling self-assessment with a rubric in hand
answer_d: Guide the construction of the conflict during re-editing, modeling the expected standard concerning the construction of the conflict

question: A high school teacher proposes to work with the students on the identification of pronouns referring to different entities. To achieve this, the teacher provides a table classifying personal, demonstrative, and possessive pronouns, and suggests reading the following short story: Fear of Reality From Monday to Friday, he would take the subway. He would travel all the lines and connections for hours. He knew every station guard. How much longer will he keep lying, they would say to him. Why doesn't he just tell her that he was fired months ago. (Paola Rivera). After the reading, the teacher asks the students about pronouns that refer to entities in the story. A student claims that the word "las" relates to one of the central elements of the story. What difficulty does the student's response reveal in relation to what the teacher requested?
answer_a: The distinction between the form of pronouns and other grammatical categories
answer_b: The identification of the entities by relating the word "las" with the word "stations"
answer_c: The lack of knowledge of the central entities of the story in question: the guards, him, the wife
answer_d: The conceptual recognition of the different types of pronouns and their specific characteristics

question:
A high school teacher works with students on reading, analyzing, and interpreting lyrical texts related to the theme of freedom. In an activity, they listen to the song “El cautivo de Til Til” and are then asked to analyze and characterize the lyrical speaker based on the following excerpt:
They say Manuel is his name
and they take him on the road to Til Til,
that the governor does not want
to see his genteel bearing along La Cañada.
They say that in war he was
the best and in the city
he dazzled like the lightning
of freedom.
(...)
They say he was like lightning
when he rode his steed
and that as the rider passed
all called him by the name Manuel.
I don’t know if I will return
to see him free and genteel,
I only know he smiled on the way
to Til Til.
El cautivo de Til Til, version by Aquelarre.
Upon reviewing the activity, the teacher comes across the following student response:
“The speaker seems to be reflecting and remembering to himself. He is somewhat sad and melancholic, but he is brave, like the lightning of freedom. This comparison made by the speaker seems very interesting to me because lightning is something that dazzles and so is freedom. He mentions the name of a place in Chile, and in general, he does not use difficult words.”
What problem does the student's response present in relation to the purpose of the activity proposed by the teacher?
answer_a: It shows a partial confusion between the subject dealt with and the voice expressed in the text
answer_b: It develops a response that strays from what was asked in the activity, as it focuses on other elements of the poem
answer_c: It focuses on personal appreciations over the content of the lyrical text to characterize the speaker
answer_d: It shows a lack of relevant references to the text in the response, as it only refers to a comparison made in it, but not with other verses

question: A teacher of 2nd grade of secondary school tackles the writing of expository texts. During the activity, he reviews the following statements from texts written by his students: "They have made all efforts to reduce gas emissions, therefore, they have not achieved it" and "No visible changes have been made in the organic waste treatment method, and monetary contributions have arrived to implement them." What is the main difficulty evident in the texts presented by the students?
answer_a: The impossibility of establishing connectors to advance in writing
answer_b: The lack of connectors in general in their different semantic relations
answer_c: The lack of knowledge of semantic relations for textual construction
answer_d: The incorrect use of connectors to establish relations of opposition between ideas

question:
Read the following excerpt from an essay submitted by a second-year high school student:
In the novel, one can see the lack of freedom experienced by the characters, especially the protagonist, to do what they want or act according to their true desires. For example, at one point the narrator says that no one can marry someone they truly love because if they are caught they could be imprisoned or executed. This seems very bad to me because one cannot be free even to be with the person they want and, sometimes, in today's society, this can be seen, for example, when people are pressured or pressure themselves to be with someone out of convenience or for appearances or money and not for love.
Which of the following possible comments from a teacher on the student's essay would be appropriate feedback for the use of citations in writing?
answer_a: If you do not include textual citations, your arguments will lose validity
answer_b: Extend the paragraph with another aspect of the problem and support it with a textual citation from the novel
answer_c: If instead of referencing the novel you add a textual citation, the point you want to discuss would be more explicit
answer_d: Re-read the guide that explains what citations consist of and carefully look at the examples presented

question: A teacher, who is working on argumentation with a year 3 high school class, reviews the following writing from one of her students: “Expert advisors have stated that, currently, we find ourselves with the highest gas emission index in the last three years.” Which of the following statements would constitute the most appropriate feedback to correct the agreement error presented by the term “highest” in the previous writing?
answer_a: The passage presents a grammatical disagreement in the term "highest"
answer_b: The text must be corrected, as it has a number agreement error in the word "highest"
answer_c: With what element does the adjective "highest" agree in grammatical number?
answer_d: You should read your text again, find the grammatical error and rewrite it correctly

question: A kindergarten teacher requires conducting a diagnostic assessment to explore the lexical skills of children, specifically the ability to define words and recognize which category they belong to.  What educational situation is appropriate to gather evidence regarding these skills?
answer_a: Invite the children to play guessing games. Essential characteristics of different words will be mentioned, without using visual support. Use a checklist to record performance
answer_b: Present the children with a series of objects and baskets representing different categories, and invite them to select one of the objects, mention its name, and place it in a category. Assess performance using a rubric
answer_c: Invite the children to observe a double-entry table containing some categories, and provide a series of cards that they must associate with the corresponding category. Use anecdotal records to document performance
answer_d: Present the children with sheets containing images of different categories, and ask them to select one and describe it without mentioning its name. Peers should describe the word and mention its category. Evaluate performance using a rating scale

question: A fourth grade teacher is reading with his students the following excerpt from the story *The Discussion of the Hares,* by Alicia Morel:  Simon the rabbit had a ferocious appetite. He also had a wife, Clarita, and a large family of eight children, because they were "multilittered." On a sunny winter day, one of those where you feel like running and flying across fields and mountains, Simon called his wife to take the family out for fresh air. "Clarita, take advantage of the good weather because it's going to rain tomorrow!" "Are you crazy? Dogs or the fox that lives in the nearby forest could come," she replied, barely poking her nose out of the burrow. "What dogs or foxes! Today is truce day." "Are you sure?" "I'm not brave enough to be up here if today wasn't the day when no hunter can hunt," Simon affirmed, lying back to soak up the sun.  Which of the following questions can the teacher ask for students to make an inference from the text?
answer_a: What was the weather like the day Simon called his wife?
answer_b: What did you think of Simon's attitude towards Clarita?
answer_c: Why did Simon want his wife to take the kids out that day?
answer_d: What feeling does Clarita convey when she replies to her husband?

question: A second-grade teacher worked on the story of Cinderella with their class and then conducted a brief assessment of the students' levels of understanding. One of the questions the teacher asked was: “Why did Cinderella's stepsisters insist on trying on the glass slipper even though it didn’t fit them well?”  What evaluation indicator is addressed through the question asked by the teacher?
answer_a: They recognize the conflict in narrative texts
answer_b: They establish cause relationships in narrative texts
answer_c: They identify sequences of events in narrative texts
answer_d: They identify characteristics of secondary characters in narrative texts

question: A teacher of a 4th grade class is designing a test to assess the reading comprehension of her students through various questions related to non-literary texts. Among the selected texts, the teacher includes the following:  Bats are the only mammals equipped with wings capable of flying. One of their characteristics is that they have a very limited sense of sight, so they orient themselves and locate obstacles and food using a developed system of high-frequency ultrasounds inaudible to humans.  They are nocturnal animals that feed on insects and small animals. Like bees and other insects, bats fulfill an important function in nature: they are pollinators without which many plant species could not reproduce.  Although bats are commonly associated with being small animals, there are bats of different sizes. The smallest weighs about 1.5 grams, while the largest can weigh 1.2 kilograms and have a wingspan of 1.5 meters.  Bats are present on all continents, except Antarctica. Like mole rats, they are mammals whose body temperature depends on the environment, especially when inactive.  (Adapted from: www.nationalgeographic.com.es/animales/murcielagos).  Which of the following questions allows evaluating the extraction of implicit information from the previous text?
answer_a: Why aren't bats found in Antarctica?
answer_b: Why are bats commonly associated with being small animals?
answer_c: What characteristic distinguishes bats from other mammals?
answer_d: Why can't humans hear the sounds bats make?

question: Which of the following strategies is appropriate for 4th grade students to practice recognizing the meanings that affixes add to the words they modify?
answer_a: Read the text: "The little prince was capricious and disobedient. He had to be given everything he wanted because the king, his father, said that nothing should be denied to the son of a king". Then answer: Why is it said that the little prince was capricious and disobedient?
answer_b: Read the text: "Scientists are studying what is happening with the immense ice masses of Antarctica to see how they can affect the planet and cause an increasingly unstable climate". Then answer: What does the underlined term in the text mean?
answer_c: Read the text: "The Aurora of Chile is very important because it helped promote independence ideals. Many Chileans, by reading this newspaper, were convinced that an independent Chile from Spain was possible". Then answer: What did the Chileans become convinced of when reading the Aurora of Chile newspaper?
answer_d: Read the text: "On Sunday, the London Zoo reopened, a day after the fire that forced activities to be suspended. The London Zoo, the oldest in the world, opened its doors for the first time in 1826 and houses more than

question: A third grade teacher reads the following text written by one of her students: "I had a great time during the long weekend. I went to the new science museum and then took a tour and saw a real lizard. Then I saw a movie about the planets, went to the store and bought a book, went home and read it all." Which of the following morphosyntactic aspects should be corrected in the student's text?
answer_a: Use of connectors
answer_b: Use of definite and indefinite articles
answer_c: Verb conjugations
answer_d: Grammatical agreement

question: Which of the following activities specifically allows working on grammatical agreement in writing with 2nd Grade students?
answer_a: Play drawing what a sentence says. For example, if the sentence says: “The rose has thorns”, draw a rose with thorns
answer_b: Play describing features of characters from an image. For example, from the image of a clown, point out the color of their clothes, the makeup on their face, etc
answer_c: Play identifying mistakes in the language of an alien. For example, from the sentence “The dog drank the milk”, identify the alien's mistakes
answer_d: Play creating absurd sentences from given words. For example, a student receives a card with the word “bread” and creates a nonsensical sentence, like: “I wore a blue bread.”

question: A teacher of middle-level children has observed that her group of boys and girls enjoys creative and exploratory experiences using their hands, and often copies letters from stories, magazines, and logos. Therefore, at the beginning of the second semester, she proposes to work on the following learning objectives:  - Verbal Language Core: "Produce their own graphic signs in playful situations."  - Corporality and Movement Core: "Perfect their fine visuomotor coordination through the use of various objects, toys, and utensils."  What learning experience promotes the objectives defined by the teacher?
answer_a: In a large group, conduct a shared reading of poems; subsequently, the children copy some words creating their own messages
answer_b: In small groups, the children are invited to cut out words from magazines and newspapers, and then to copy some of them creating new texts
answer_c: In small groups, the children are invited to collaboratively write a recipe, and then cook using spoons, whisks, and bowls to make the mixture
answer_d: In a large group, conduct a story reading aloud and then invite the children to draw the cover or scenes from the story while copying the name of the characters

question: In a higher nursery level, the educational team decides to plan strategies to promote the following learning objective of the Verbal Language core: “To express orally their needs and interests, through the combination of words and gestures, the use of word-phrase and progressively the use of simple sentences.”  Which set of activities is appropriate for the children to address this learning objective?
answer_a: In the initial circle, ask the children to repeat words from a song. Then, in a new experience, have them follow songs with physical and verbal response. They finish by singing accompanied by percussion instruments
answer_b: In small groups, ask the children to identify and repeat onomatopoeias of different animals. Then, in a new experience, have them repeat rhymes related to animals. They finish by completing simple sentences with rhymes related to animals
answer_c: In large groups, invite the children to explore and taste a fruit juice and motivate them to discover its ingredients through riddles. Then, in a new experience, invite them to select by naming the fruits they wish to use to prepare a new juice to taste
answer_d: During the reading of a story, ask the children to say who their favorite character is. Then, in a new experience, have them color a stick puppet with their favorite character, and ask them to present it to their classmates. Finish by encouraging them to play with the puppet and create stories freely

question: A preschool teacher plans to evaluate the following learning objective from the Verbal Language core: "To express oneself orally in a clear and understandable manner, using complete sentence structures, appropriate and precise verb conjugations with respect to tenses, persons, and communicative intentions." To this end, she designs a learning experience in which the children must create a story from a sequence of three images, which will be recorded by the teacher. Isabel, age 5, narrates the following story: "Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a llana (frog) and a pello (dog) and the boy had fallen asleep on the bed and the llana (frog) got out of the jar and was gone, and he caught it. The end."  Considering the expected performances in expressive language for a child of this level, what feature of Isabel's story shows that she has not yet achieved the indicated learning?
answer_a: She does not include adjectives in the sentences
answer_b: She does not include adverbs in the sentences
answer_c: She does not conjugate verbs in the past perfect tense
answer_d: She does not correctly articulate the trilled 'r' sound

question: A 3rd grade teacher is going to work on writing a story with her students, focusing on the adaptation to the communicative situation. Considering this focus of the activity, which of the following questions the teacher asks would be most appropriate for the students to begin planning their textual production?
answer_a: What will our story be about?
answer_b: For whom will we write our story?
answer_c: Where will the story of our tale take place?
answer_d: What type of language will we use in our story?

question: Based on an experimental activity, a third-grade student wrote the following text, in which he explains what happens to the seeds six days after being placed in a moist substrate.  May 12.  With the moist corns, after 6 days, leaves appeared and they can now perform photosynthesis.  Which grammatical aspect needs correcting in the student's writing?
answer_a: The use of connectors according to their functions
answer_b: The number agreement between article and noun
answer_c: The use of verb conjugation according to tenses
answer_d: The number agreement between the pronoun and the noun it replaces

question: A 4th grade teacher is reviewing the written text productions by his students, based on an assignment where he asked them to write a family anecdote. A student submitted the following piece:  Family Anecdote  Saturday was a great day. I went out with my mom and grandparents to eat Chinese food. I loved it! When we arrived at the restaurant, we took a table for four and requested the menu to see the options. There were two choices, menu A and B. We ordered B, because it included a greater variety of dishes. Once we decided, my mom told me, “Martina, place the order.” So I called the waiter and ordered menu B and a drink for each of us. I felt like a grown-up!  What idiomatic correction should the teacher make in the student's text?
answer_a: Formation of the plural of the noun "menu."
answer_b: Conjugation of the verb "hacer" (to do/make) regarding person and verb mood
answer_c: Impersonal conjugation of the verb "haber" in the sentence: “There were two options, menu A and B.”
answer_d: Use of the first person singular in the sentence: “I went out with my mom and grandparents to eat Chinese food.”

question: A teacher in a 6th grade class is exercising reading comprehension with the students. As part of the activities, she has them read the following poem with the goal of interpretation:  Butterfly of the air,   how beautiful you are,   butterfly of the air   golden and green.   Light of a lantern,   butterfly of the air   stay there, there, there!   Stay there!   Butterfly, are you there?    (Butterfly, Federico García Lorca).  What reading comprehension strategy would be appropriate to apply after the reading to achieve the proposed objective?
answer_a: Answer the question: what is the lyrical reason of the poem?
answer_b: Answer the question: where do you think the butterfly went?
answer_c: Share with classmates what they know about butterflies
answer_d: Mark the terms that talk about the butterfly and relate them to the poem

question: A teacher of an 8th-grade class will work with students on the following objective: "Develop investigations by adequately evaluating the consulted sources of information." To do this, a project is proposed which consists of choosing an author of their interest to research about their work and then present the work to their classmates.  Which of the following activities promotes in students the appropriate search for information for the realization of the indicated projects?
answer_a: Ask them to review the information they have in relation to their objectives to find quotes that support their conclusions
answer_b: Guide the search for information based on the formulation of questions about any of their books, for example: how is the author's particular style reflected in this work?
answer_c: Look for books by the chosen authors or, if they have not chosen, suggest one based on a genre of their interest to have a broader view of the theme
answer_d: Propose the use of a checklist in the texts found, based on indicators such as: "Is it written clearly?", "Does it identify its author or responsible institution?", "Does it present technical language about the topic?"

question: In a 7th grade classroom, during the unit on Myths and creation stories, a teacher is working on the following learning objective: "Analyze the role of characters in creation myths." To achieve this, he has chosen a selection of stories created by different cultures.  Which of the following activities is suitable for students to address this objective?
answer_a: Create cards mentioning the characters of each myth and the culture to which they belong
answer_b: Create diagrams distinguishing main, secondary, and incidental characters from the selected myths
answer_c: Create tables in which they relate some characters from each myth with the realities explained in these narratives
answer_d: Write brief texts in which they inform about the characteristics of the main characters of the selected myths

question: After an activity in which the 8th grade students had to write an informative text, the teacher realized that most of the class has problems using co-reference, as they incur in lexical repetition and do not use other mechanisms, such as pronouns or deictics, among others.  What remedial strategy proposed by the teacher would help the students reinforce the use of co-reference in their writing?
answer_a: Review again the different classes of words that can be used to apply co-reference in a text
answer_b: Provide students, as a review, a guide with lists of synonyms, pronouns, and deictics, including examples of their use
answer_c: Conduct a peer correction in which each student corrects a classmate's text, paying special attention to the co-reference mechanisms used by them
answer_d: Return the text to each student with marks on each repetition and ask them to rewrite it, replacing the repetitions with words that maintain the meaning of each statement

question: During the poetry unit in 8th grade, a teacher has students read the following fragment of a poem so that they can recognize the relationship between the formal aspects and the content of the poem.  Alamedas  The branch of the poplar rows above   the branch rows, we row   beneath the leaves, we fly   up the sap, mast ascended.   The leaves row through the torrent   of the avenue. Come, then, feel   how it dives among the skies   the green arms towards the west. (Rafael Rubio).  Which of the following questions would allow students to relate the predominant figure with the meaning of the poem?
answer_a: What rhetorical figures are used in the poem?
answer_b: How does the style of versification relate to the title of the poem?
answer_c: Is there any relationship between the sounds and what happens in the poem?
answer_d: What function does the meter serve in the distribution and understanding of the poem?

question: A teacher, in an 8th grade, at the end of the unit on Dramatic Genre, asks the students to create a brief text. Upon reviewing them, he finds the following creation of a student:  A house like any other. On the right, the son in the room playing on the computer, and on the left, the dad preparing tea.  DAD: Son, come have tea. This is the tenth time I've told you.  SON: I'm coming, give me a few minutes.  DAD: (Very angry) Come immediately!  SON: Yes, I'm coming, I'm just finishing a match of Free Fire.  But the dad can't take it anymore and goes angrily to talk to his son, to tell him how it's possible that he is so obsessed that he no longer spends time with his father.  SON: But dad, it’s for my future. I will be a gaming influencer! -the dad stays in the room watching his son thoughtfully-.  DAD: I just wanted to share with you the only time we can be together.  SON: Oh, I'm sorry! Just give me 5 minutes and I'll go.  And this is how another day ends in an ordinary family.  What difficulty in the process of learning to produce dramatic texts is noted in the student’s creation?
answer_a: Mixes the stage directions language with the aside
answer_b: Confuses the aside with the dialogue of the characters
answer_c: Confuses the voice of the characters with the voice of the narrator
answer_d: Does not understand the function of stage directions in a dramatic work

question: A teacher is working on punctuation with his 7th grade students. To do this, he hands out a guide that contains the following exercise:  Read the following fragment and place the comma, when appropriate, in the underlined segment.  Sergio Gómez is a columnist, editor, Spanish teacher, and Chilean writer who owes his fame mainly to the juvenile novels he has written, particularly the series of the teenage detective Quique Hache.  The students correctly complete the activity by placing the comma in the underlined segment after the words: columnist and editor.  What prior learning do the students need to correctly apply the comma in the underlined segment?
answer_a: Recognize analogous syntactic elements
answer_b: Identify adjective subordinate clauses
answer_c: Identify the vocative within a sentence
answer_d: Distinguish conjunctive elements within a sentence

question: During the Poetry unit in a 6th-grade class, in an evaluation context, a teacher asks the students to read the following excerpt from a poem by Nicanor Parra, so they can analyze it, identifying elements of poetic language.
